summary: Intra-weight injection lets one model change another model's behaviour by editing its weights directly, without gradients. Such edits can range from altering lexical associations to enforcing output formats or updating factual knowledge.
takeaways: Despite growing interest in these approaches, there has been no systematic way to evaluate how well models perform them.
Editors are limited to four tools for reading and writing weights, with bounded tensor access and a fixed budget for generating and inspecting rollouts.
Evaluating frontier closed- and open-weight models reveals sharply diverging capabilities, both across models and across tasks.
